intro: Adding vectors that point different ways.

widget.instructions: The amber arrow is a + b, drawn tip to tail. Drag the tips to explore; Reset restores the question's vectors.

stem: Vector a has magnitude {{a}} units pointing east. Vector b has magnitude {{b}} units pointing north.
What is the magnitude of a + b?

hints.text: Place b's tail at a's tip. The resultant runs from a's tail to b's tip.
The two vectors are at right angles, so they form the two shorter sides of a right triangle.

magnitudes-added.text: Magnitudes only add when the vectors point the same way. These are at right angles: use Pythagoras.

magnitudes-subtracted.text: Subtracting magnitudes works only for opposite vectors. These are perpendicular.

generic.text: Draw them tip to tail and find the length of the hypotenuse.

workedSolution.text: Tip to tail, a and b form a right triangle with the resultant as its hypotenuse.
|a + b| = √({{a}}² + {{b}}²) = √{{ss}} = {{R}} units, at {{ang}}° north of east.

magnitudes-added.front: Do vector magnitudes add when the vectors are perpendicular?
magnitudes-added.back: No. |a + b| = √(a² + b²) for perpendicular vectors.

magnitudes-subtracted.back: Only when a and b point in opposite directions.
